Thanks Ben — Lina / Dustin, copying in a concise technical summary below you can use in the SIG/SOC2 response. I'll also attach a sample manifest and a one-week export blob for your reviewers.

What we log (canonical admin event fields):
- event_id (UUID)
- timestamp_utc (ISO8601, normalized to UTC; original_tz retained in original_timestamp field)
- actor_user_id (internal user id or service principal)
- actor_display_name (human-readable)
- actor_role (role at time of action: admin, superadmin, operator)
- action_type (API_CALL | CONSOLE_ACTION | TOKEN_CREATE | ROLE_CHANGE | PRIV_ACTION)
- target_resource (resource id / path e.g., model/<id>, deployment/<id>, project/<id>)
- request_id (correlation id)
- ip_address (source IP), geo_location (derived; country/region)
- session_id (if available), device_fingerprint (if available)
- request_payload_summary (redacted summary)
- response_status (HTTP code or internal result)
- change_diff (JSON-diff string when applicable)
- audit_flags (e.g., elevated_privilege, exported)

Retention and legal hold options:
- Hosted (default): 12 months of full-fidelity admin events retained.
- Dedicated: configurable retention up to 5 years under reserve contracts.
- Private (VPC/on-prem): retention set by customer; we can provide tooling and runbook to snapshot on request.
- Legal hold: we support preserved snapshots (immutable) on a per-tenant basis; hold snapshots are retained until released by authorized contacts.

Export formats and packaging:
- Preferred: compressed Parquet (partitioned by date) + top-level manifest.json with per-chunk SHA256 and HMAC-SHA256 signatures. Parquet provides efficient columnar ingest for SIEM and analytics.
- Alternate: newline-delimited JSON (JSONL) gzip; CSV (for limited schema export).
- Bundle: we produce a zipped envelope with manifest, chunk checksums, and a short human-readable README describing schema and sample queries.

Delivery handshake and integrity:
- Delivery options: S3 (pre-signed PUT or presigned GET for pull), SFTP (key-based), secure rsync over SSH (for Private).
- Manifest: signed manifest.json that lists chunk file names, SHA256 checksums, record counts, time range, and a manifest_signature (HMAC-SHA256 using a per-export ephemeral key).
- Signing: we can rotate keys per-export and provide the ephemeral public verification artifact via a signed token. If required, we can provide a PGP-signed manifest instead.

Timezones and timestamps:
- We normalize all stored timestamps to UTC (timestamp_utc) and include original_timestamp with timezone offset so auditors can reconcile logs. Timestamps in exports follow UTC by default.

On-demand vs scheduled pulls and SLA:
- Scheduled: daily or weekly snapshots (configurable).
- On-demand: typical turnaround 3 business days for hosted accounts to prepare export with manifest and signed attestation. Expedited 1–2 day options available for Dedicated customers.

Security controls on export:
- All exported artifacts are encrypted at rest (server-side SSE-KMS for S3), and in transit using TLS.
- Access control: exports bound to requester's account and require approval by a designated admin. Detailed audit entry is created for export requests.

Next steps (proposal):
1) We produce a 1-week sample (2026-09-01 to 2026-09-07) as Parquet + manifest; upload to s3://redwood-evidence/acmehealth/2026-10/admin-activity-sample/ and provide time-limited presigned GET links.
2) Lina confirms preferred delivery (S3 presigned vs SFTP) and whether Acme requires PGP-signed manifests or HMAC only.
3) Ben to coordinate any contractual retention/escrow language if Acme needs longer retention.

I'll attach sample manifest and an anonymized 500-line JSONL snippet for quick review.

—Karthik
